title: Short-term risk of serious fall injuries in older adults initiating and intensifying treatment with antihypertensive medication
authors: Shimbo D, Barrett Bowling C, Levitan EB, Deng L, Sim JJ, Huang L, et al.
population: Medicare beneficiaries aged 65 or older with a serious fall injury identified from emergency department and inpatient claims; case-crossover design comparing the 15 days before the fall with six earlier 15-day control periods
funder: This work was supported by the National Institutes of Health (K24-HL125704) from the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, Bethesda, MD.
authorConflicts: Muntner and Levitan have received institutional grants from Amgen Inc, stated as unrelated to the topic.
result: 272, 1508 and 3113 beneficiaries initiated, added a new class or titrated antihypertensive treatment within 15 days before a serious fall injury. Odds of a serious fall injury were raised in the 15 days after initiation (odds ratio 1.36, 95% CI 1.19 to 1.55), after adding a new class (1.16, 1.10 to 1.23) and after titration (1.13, 1.08 to 1.18); associations were attenuated beyond 15 days and did not vary by medication class.
